title: Board Evidence Windows on the Evidence Submission and Hearing Dockets — Decision Reviews and Appeals
content:
### Board practice: the evidence window (Decision Reviews and Appeals)

**Rule of practice.** On the Evidence Submission Docket, evidence counts only if it is received within 90 days after the Board receives the notice of disagreement; on the Hearing Docket, only at the hearing or within 90 days after it. Evidence received outside the window is not considered by the Board and may instead support a new supplemental claim. Lanes that take no evidence never record evidence as considered.

**The window in each lane of Decision Reviews and Appeals**

| Lane | Window (calendar days) | The window runs from |
|---|---|---|
| Supplemental Claim | 0 | No Board window is run |
| Higher-Level Review | 0 | No Board window is run |
| Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference | 0 | No Board window is run |
| Board Appeal - Direct Review Docket | 0 | No Board window is run |
| Board Appeal - Evidence Submission Docket | 90 | The Board's receipt of the notice of disagreement |
| Board Appeal - Hearing Docket | 90 | The hearing date; evidence presented at the hearing itself also counts |

**How evidence appears on the record.** Each receipt of evidence for a review is recorded by kind of evidence and date received, and is marked as inside or outside the docket's window; evidence received in a regional office lane that takes evidence is marked as inside. Evidence received outside the window is not considered by the Board, on any docket. The Higher-Level Review lanes and the Direct Review Docket take no evidence, so no evidence is ever recorded as considered in them.

**Applying the rule to hypothetical receipts**

| Docket | Hypothetical receipt | Counts for the Board | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence Submission Docket | A medical opinion received 30 days after the Board receives the notice of disagreement | Yes | Within the 90-day window |
| Evidence Submission Docket | Private medical records received 120 days after the Board receives the notice of disagreement | No | Outside the window; may instead support a new supplemental claim |
| Hearing Docket | A lay statement presented at the hearing | Yes | Received at the hearing |
| Hearing Docket | Service records received 45 days after the hearing | Yes | Within the 90-day window after the hearing |
| Hearing Docket | Financial records received 150 days after the hearing | No | Outside the window; may instead support a new supplemental claim |
| Direct Review Docket | Any evidence | No | The lane takes no evidence |

**Notes on the rule**

- The two windows are of the same length but are anchored differently: the Evidence Submission Docket counts from the Board's receipt of the notice of disagreement, the Hearing Docket from the hearing.
- Evidence received outside the window is not considered by the Board; it may instead support a new supplemental claim.
